text.p: Following are the reports carried by Estonia's newspapers on Monday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Estonian Prime Minister Tiit Vaehi and Foreign Minister Toomas Ilves say they are satisfied with the results of the Dublin summit.
- The Union of the Russian Citizens in Estonia approved a resolution demanding official status for the Russian language in areas with a Russian population.
- Hardo Pajula, soon to leave his post as economic counsellor to the prime minister, forecasts a setback to Estonia's economy, saying its success is being based on myth about the country's progress.
- Heavy snowfall delayed air and railroad traffic and seriously hampered city traffic in Tallinn. The rescue service urged people to stay home and avoid travel by car.
- The Bank of Estonia limits to 20 the number of one kroon coins allowed to be taken out of the country to prevent them being used illegally in slot machines in Germany.
- Estonia may lose a Korean investment for the establishment of a Hyundai bus factory because of insufficient interest in the project from officials.
